Recursion is a programming technique where a function solves a problem by calling itself with a smaller or simpler version of the same problem. Each recursive call works on a reduced case until it reaches a **base case**, which is a simple condition that stops further calls and returns a result. By combining the results from each step as the calls unwind, the original problem is solved. Think of it like a set of nested Russian dolls: you keep opening smaller dolls (calls) until you reach the tiniest one (base case), then you put them back together in reverse order.
